NIS2:Art. 20(1).title: Governance: management approves and oversees the security measures
NIS2:Art. 20(1).note: Evidence that the management body formally approves the cybersecurity risk-management measures, oversees how they are rolled out, and accepts accountability for them (the Implementing Regulation's annex 1.1, 1.2 and 2.3 add detail for digital-infrastructure entities).

NIS2:Art. 20(2).title: Governance: cybersecurity training for management bodies
NIS2:Art. 20(2).note: Evidence that members of the management body take regular training that lets them judge cybersecurity risks and the organisation's practices, and that similar training is offered to staff.
NIS2:Art. 20(2).source: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), OJ L 333, 27.12.2022, p. 80 (CELEX 32022L2555); id as numbered in the Directive; the Directive has no headings below article level, so the title is the project's short description of the paragraph or list point; ISO 27001 links are the project's own judgement (no ENISA mapping for this point); EU AI Act links are the project's own judgement; the note is the project's own wording

NIS2:Art. 21(1).title: Appropriate and proportionate cybersecurity risk-management measures
NIS2:Art. 21(1).note: Evidence that technical, operational and organisational security measures are chosen in proportion to the organisation's risk exposure, size and incident impact, to protect its network and information systems and their users.
NIS2:Art. 21(1).source: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), OJ L 333, 27.12.2022, p. 80 (CELEX 32022L2555); id as numbered in the Directive; the Directive has no headings below article level, so the title is the project's short description of the paragraph or list point; ISO 27001 links are the project's own judgement (no ENISA mapping for this point); EU AI Act links are the project's own judgement; the note is the project's own wording

NIS2:Art. 21(2)(a).title: Policies on risk analysis and information system security
NIS2:Art. 21(2)(a).note: Evidence of a maintained risk-analysis process and an information-system security policy that management approves and reviews (Implementing Regulation annex 1 and 2).
NIS2:Art. 21(2)(a).source: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), OJ L 333, 27.12.2022, p. 80 (CELEX 32022L2555); id as numbered in the Directive; the Directive has no headings below article level, so the title is the project's short description of the paragraph or list point; annex section named in the note is from Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690, OJ L, 18.10.2024 (CELEX 32024R2690); ISO 27001 links come from the official crosswalk in ENISA Technical Implementation Guidance on Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690, mapping table v1.2 of 21.08.2025 (annex section -> Annex A ids) (annex 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 2.2, 2.3 combined); EU AI Act links are the project's own judgement; the note is the project's own wording

NIS2:Art. 21(2)(b).title: Incident handling
NIS2:Art. 21(2)(b).note: Evidence of an incident-handling process covering monitoring and logging, reporting of events, assessment, response and post-incident review (Implementing Regulation annex 3).

NIS2:Art. 21(2)(c).title: Business continuity, backup, disaster recovery and crisis management
NIS2:Art. 21(2)(c).note: Evidence of business continuity, disaster recovery, backup and crisis-management plans that are kept current and recovery-tested (Implementing Regulation annex 4; annex 13 on utilities and physical threats also applies).

NIS2:Art. 21(2)(d).title: Supply chain security, including direct suppliers and service providers
NIS2:Art. 21(2)(d).note: Evidence that the security of suppliers and service providers is managed through a policy, a supplier directory and security terms in contracts (Implementing Regulation annex 5).
NIS2:Art. 21(2)(d).source: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), OJ L 333, 27.12.2022, p. 80 (CELEX 32022L2555); id as numbered in the Directive; the Directive has no headings below article level, so the title is the project's short description of the paragraph or list point; annex section named in the note is from Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690, OJ L, 18.10.2024 (CELEX 32024R2690); ISO 27001 links come from the official crosswalk in ENISA Technical Implementation Guidance on Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690, mapping table v1.2 of 21.08.2025 (annex section -> Annex A ids) (annex 5.1 and 5.2 combined); EU AI Act links are the project's own judgement; the note is the project's own wording

NIS2:Art. 21(2)(e).title: Security in systems acquisition, development, maintenance and vulnerabilities
NIS2:Art. 21(2)(e).note: Evidence of security requirements when buying or building systems, secure development, change and patch management, testing, network security and a vulnerability handling and disclosure process (Implementing Regulation annex 6).

NIS2:Art. 21(2)(f).title: Assessing the effectiveness of cybersecurity risk-management measures
NIS2:Art. 21(2)(f).note: Evidence of a routine for checking whether the security measures work, such as audits, testing and metrics, with results reported to management (Implementing Regulation annex 7).

NIS2:Art. 21(2)(g).title: Basic cyber hygiene practices and cybersecurity training
NIS2:Art. 21(2)(g).note: Evidence of staff awareness, basic cyber hygiene practices and role-appropriate security training (Implementing Regulation annex 8).
NIS2:Art. 21(2)(g).source: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), OJ L 333, 27.12.2022, p. 80 (CELEX 32022L2555); id as numbered in the Directive; the Directive has no headings below article level, so the title is the project's short description of the paragraph or list point; annex section named in the note is from Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690, OJ L, 18.10.2024 (CELEX 32024R2690); ISO 27001 links come from the official crosswalk in ENISA Technical Implementation Guidance on Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690, mapping table v1.2 of 21.08.2025 (annex section -> Annex A ids) (annex 8.1 and 8.2 combined); EU AI Act links are the project's own judgement; the note is the project's own wording

NIS2:Art. 21(2)(h).title: Cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption
NIS2:Art. 21(2)(h).note: Evidence of a policy that sets when and how cryptography and encryption are used, including key management (Implementing Regulation annex 9).
NIS2:Art. 21(2)(h).source: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), OJ L 333, 27.12.2022, p. 80 (CELEX 32022L2555); id as numbered in the Directive; the Directive has no headings below article level, so the title is the project's short description of the paragraph or list point; annex section named in the note is from Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690, OJ L, 18.10.2024 (CELEX 32024R2690); ISO 27001 links come from the official crosswalk in ENISA Technical Implementation Guidance on Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690, mapping table v1.2 of 21.08.2025 (annex section -> Annex A ids) (annex 9.1); EU AI Act links are the project's own judgement; the note is the project's own wording

NIS2:Art. 21(2)(i).title: Human resources security, access control and asset management
NIS2:Art. 21(2)(i).note: Evidence of staff vetting and leaver handling, access control with least privilege, and a classified asset inventory (Implementing Regulation annex 10, 11, 12 and 13); this one point bundles three topics and could be split.

NIS2:Art. 21(2)(j).title: Multi-factor authentication and secured communications
NIS2:Art. 21(2)(j).note: Evidence that multi-factor or continuous authentication and secured voice, video, text and emergency communications are used where appropriate (Implementing Regulation annex 11.7 covers multi-factor only; it has no section on secured communications).

NIS2:Art. 21(3).title: Supplier vulnerabilities and quality when choosing supply chain measures
NIS2:Art. 21(3).note: Evidence that supplier choices take into account each direct supplier's known vulnerabilities, product quality and secure development practice, and any EU-level coordinated supply chain risk assessment.

NIS2:Art. 21(4).title: Corrective measures when the Art. 21(2) measures are not met
NIS2:Art. 21(4).note: Evidence that when a gap against the Art. 21(2) measures is found, corrective action is taken without undue delay and tracked to closure (Implementing Regulation annex 2.3 has corrective actions on review results).
NIS2:Art. 21(4).source: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), OJ L 333, 27.12.2022, p. 80 (CELEX 32022L2555); id as numbered in the Directive; the Directive has no headings below article level, so the title is the project's short description of the paragraph or list point; annex section named in the note is from Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690, OJ L, 18.10.2024 (CELEX 32024R2690); ISO 27001 links are the project's own judgement (no ENISA mapping for this point); EU AI Act links are the project's own judgement; the note is the project's own wording

NIS2:Art. 23(1).title: Notifying the CSIRT or authority of significant incidents
NIS2:Art. 23(1).note: Evidence that the organisation can tell which incidents are significant for it and notifies its CSIRT or competent authority without undue delay, and affected service recipients where appropriate (Implementing Regulation Art. 3 sets criteria for in-scope digital entities).
NIS2:Art. 23(1).source: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), OJ L 333, 27.12.2022, p. 80 (CELEX 32022L2555); id as numbered in the Directive; the Directive has no headings below article level, so the title is the project's short description of the paragraph or list point; annex section named in the note is from Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690, OJ L, 18.10.2024 (CELEX 32024R2690); ISO 27001 links are the project's own judgement (no ENISA mapping for this point); EU AI Act links are the project's own judgement; the note is the project's own wording

NIS2:Art. 23(2).title: Informing service recipients of significant cyber threats
NIS2:Art. 23(2).note: Evidence that recipients of the service who may be affected by a significant cyber threat are told what measures or remedies they can apply, and of the threat itself where appropriate.
NIS2:Art. 23(2).source: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), OJ L 333, 27.12.2022, p. 80 (CELEX 32022L2555); id as numbered in the Directive; the Directive has no headings below article level, so the title is the project's short description of the paragraph or list point; ISO 27001 links are the project's own judgement (no ENISA mapping for this point); EU AI Act links are the project's own judgement; the note is the project's own wording

NIS2:Art. 23(4)(a).title: Early warning within 24 hours
NIS2:Art. 23(4)(a).note: Evidence of a process to send an early warning within 24 hours of becoming aware of a significant incident, saying whether malicious acts are suspected or cross-border impact is possible.
NIS2:Art. 23(4)(a).source: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), OJ L 333, 27.12.2022, p. 80 (CELEX 32022L2555); id as numbered in the Directive; the Directive has no headings below article level, so the title is the project's short description of the paragraph or list point; ISO 27001 links are the project's own judgement (no ENISA mapping for this point); EU AI Act links are the project's own judgement; the note is the project's own wording

NIS2:Art. 23(4)(b).title: Incident notification within 72 hours
NIS2:Art. 23(4)(b).note: Evidence of a process to send an incident notification within 72 hours that updates the early warning with an initial assessment of severity and impact and, where known, indicators of compromise.
NIS2:Art. 23(4)(b).source: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), OJ L 333, 27.12.2022, p. 80 (CELEX 32022L2555); id as numbered in the Directive; the Directive has no headings below article level, so the title is the project's short description of the paragraph or list point; ISO 27001 links are the project's own judgement (no ENISA mapping for this point); EU AI Act links are the project's own judgement; the note is the project's own wording

NIS2:Art. 23(4)(c).title: Intermediate report on request
NIS2:Art. 23(4)(c).note: Evidence that a status-update report on an ongoing significant incident can be produced when the CSIRT or authority asks for one.
NIS2:Art. 23(4)(c).source: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), OJ L 333, 27.12.2022, p. 80 (CELEX 32022L2555); id as numbered in the Directive; the Directive has no headings below article level, so the title is the project's short description of the paragraph or list point; ISO 27001 links are the project's own judgement (no ENISA mapping for this point); EU AI Act links are the project's own judgement; the note is the project's own wording

NIS2:Art. 23(4)(d).title: Final report within one month
NIS2:Art. 23(4)(d).note: Evidence of a process to deliver a final report within one month of the incident notification (or a progress report then and a final one later if the incident is still ongoing), covering root cause, mitigation and impact.
